idle: Offside is simple. Give me a napkin.
First woman in the ILHL. Write it down. I have.
good_ice: Clean ice, clean calls. I love this job.
bad_ice: The roof drip on the home blue line. Again.
If the puck hops over a stick, that's the ice, not me.
wet_ice: Delay. Wet ice. I'm writing the time down to the minute.
cold: My coat's on the floor. It's colder down there.
hungry: Did Shauna bring crullers? Asking for three officials.
long_line: I'll be on the ice in four minutes. The line is not my problem.
bored: I could explain offside to someone. Anyone.
goal: Good goal. Onside by a skate lace. I checked.
greet_owner: Hey! I asked politely, once. This is the second time.
Owner. Good evening. The book misses you.
leaving_happy: Three games, zero complaints, and a hook. Good night.
leaving_angry: Asked politely twice. It's in the book now.

beer_league: No, I am not the girl ref. I am the ref.
figure_show: Look at those edges. That's who I watch for.
pro_practice: Dukes practice. I'm watching how they line up on the draws. For science.

first.say: Nell Haraldsen. I ref the beer league four nights a week and work the lines on Saturdays. You're the owner? Great. I have a list. It's polite.

options.text: I'd love to see the list.

first_list.say: Item one: a second coat hook. Item two: see item one. There are three officials and one hook. The incident book has asked, in my handwriting.

first_girl.say: I'm the ref. You'll know the difference when you get two minutes for asking. (She smiles. It's not a warm one yet.)

options.text: I'm sorry, Nell. I'll fix it.

hooks_done.say: Two hooks! Two! My coat has never been this dry. I've written you a line in the book. It's a nice one.

say: Twenty minutes to puck drop. I've got time for one question or one offside diagram.
Evening. Is the drip fixed? No? Noted.
Got a napkin? No? Never mind. What is it?

options.text: What do you like to watch on your nights off?
How do you get on with Marcel?
Can you explain offside to me?
Will you be reffing my games?

job.say: First woman to referee in the ILHL. I'm on the list. I sell ads at the Lakesider during the day so I can afford whistles. I own three.

events.say: Figure shows. For the edges. Those skaters do things with an edge that would make a winger cry. And Dukes practice, for how the pros line up on a draw.

gossip.say: Marcel is the best ref in the valley and the dryest man alive. And Coach Rourke from the Dukes doesn't yell. She just looks. It's worse. I love it.

rink.say: The ref room is a broom closet with one hook for three officials, and there's a roof drip on the home blue line that I can call like a penalty.

rink_better.say: Hooks, a chair, a heater. I could cry. I won't. Refs don't cry. We note.

offside.say: (She grabs a napkin and draws a blue line, a puck and three stick figures.) The puck crosses first. Skates follow. That's it. That's the whole game.

offside_again.say: (She draws a second napkin, with arrows. Then a third.) Okay. Keep this one. Study it. There will be a quiz.

path_player.say: Tuesdays and Thursdays, C division. I won't go easy on you because you own the building. I'll go easy on you because you're slow.
